bug_semantics: Apache Neethi PolicyReference.getRemoteReferencedPolicy (also reached from PolicyReference.normalize on a PolicyRegistry miss) built a java.net.URL from the caller-supplied wsp:PolicyReference URI and called URL.openConnection() with no scheme allowlist, no destination-address denylist, and default HttpURLConnection redirect following. An application that explicitly fetched a remote policy therefore issued outbound requests for arbitrary protocols (file, ftp, jar, …) and to link-local/multicast/any-local addresses (including cloud IMDS at 169.254.169.254), which is CWE-918 SSRF. CVE-2026-42404 is PUBLISHED at the Apache CNA (cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED, NVD vulnStatus=Analyzed); GHSA withdrawn_at is null and the vendor page still lists the CVE. 3.2.2 restricts schemes to http/https, rejects link-local/multicast/any-local, and disables redirect following.
flaw_origin: The unrestricted remote fetch was first written on 2007-06-18 in ee7f26a25bdb0bff6cbc611731159ba6f6f16032 (AXIS2-2451 PolicyReference patch by Nencho Lupanov, applied by Sanka Samaranayake). That commit added getRemoteReferedElement/getRemoteReferencedPolicy doing new URL(uri); url.openConnection() with no URI or address checks, and wired normalize() to call it when the registry miss. Parent 8baf24289b8a2976f7df94adac1d1470ec80be13 only looked up the registry and threw if unresolved; git grep of that tree finds no openConnection/getRemoteReferencedPolicy. 2011 refactors (71790ba Axiom removal inlining the URL open into getRemoteReferencedPolicy, 67fc47f formatting that blame on 3.2.1 attributes, a4c2610 PolicyEngine→PolicyBuilder) preserved the same unrestricted URLConnection sink and are not BICs.
